summary: This PR expands the Full Configuration Reference to cover most previously undocumented AIConfig fields and corrects the privacy section's incorrect claim that full source files are never sent to the AI provider.

pr_summary.headline: This PR expands the Full Configuration Reference to cover most previously undocumented AIConfig fields and corrects the privacy section's incorrect claim that full source files are never sent to the AI provider.

walkthrough.text: The Full Configuration Reference YAML block is reorganised into labelled sections (Provider, Budget, Safety, Output, Cache, Advanced) and extended with 25+ newly documented fields, each annotated with its type, default, and accepted range.

An introductory paragraph is added stating that every key maps 1:1 to AIConfig and that unknown keys are silently dropped with a warning; both claims are accurate per AIConfig.from_mapping (config.py:344-386).

The fix-mode privacy description is corrected: 'full files' is removed from the NOT-sent list and replaced with a new subsection explaining the 500-line FULL_FILE_THRESHOLD, the batch path behaviour, and that max_prompt_tokens is a soft budget for single-issue and refinement paths.
'Detected secrets' is added to the NOT-sent list, accurately reflecting that redact_secrets() is called on every prompt (fix_context.py:182).

Two AIConfig fields — transcript_logging and transcript_retention — are absent from the reference YAML block despite the introduction claiming all fields are shown there; they appear only in a separate prose section without type or range metadata.

verdict_reasoning.deciding_factor: The only open finding is a P3 inaccuracy: the reference block introduction claims to show all AIConfig fields, but transcript_logging and transcript_retention are missing from it (documented only in a separate prose section). No P1 or P2 issues were found — all technical claims about FULL_FILE_THRESHOLD, batch-path behaviour, the soft-budget semantics, and secret redaction were verified against the implementation and are accurate.

findings.title: Reference intro claims completeness but omits two fields
findings.description: The Full Configuration Reference introduction states 'All fields are optional; each is shown with its type, default, and accepted range,' and the PR description repeats that it 'now documents every field in lintro/ai/config.py.' Two fields present in AIConfig are not in the reference YAML block: `transcript_logging` (bool, default false) and `transcript_retention` (int ≥ 1, default 10). Both appear only in the 'Local transcript logging' prose section (lines 1063-1068) without their type, default, or accepted range, so a reader relying on the reference block for a complete picture will not find them there.
findings.cause: config.py defines transcript_logging (line 283) and transcript_retention (line 292) as full fields with Field() constraints, but neither was added to the Full Configuration Reference YAML block when the other 25+ fields were documented in this PR.
findings.fix: Add transcript_logging and transcript_retention to the '── Advanced / trust' or a new '── Transcript' section of the reference YAML block with their type, default, and range, matching the pattern used for every other field.
findings.suggested_code:
# ── Request/response transcript logging ─────────────────────
  # Write raw provider traffic as NDJSON under .lintro-cache/ai/transcripts/.
  # Off by default; also enabled by LINTRO_AI_TRANSCRIPT=1.
  # (bool, default: false)
  transcript_logging: false

  # Max transcript NDJSON files to retain; older files are pruned.
  # (int >= 1, default: 10)
  transcript_retention: 10
